headline: Twin Falls ICE flight observers record more than 500 detainees flown out of Magic Valley airport
summary: ICE conducts weekly deportation flights at Twin Falls airport since April 2026. Activists monitor and record these flights, raising concerns about due process for detainees, while a local representative supports the operations enforcing "rule of law".

headline: NJ residents share stories of masked ICE agents in push to retain mask ban
summary: New Jersey is challenging a Trump administration lawsuit aiming to overturn its law prohibiting ICE agents from wearing masks during immigration enforcement due to safety concerns. The state argues that federal agents' masked operations have caused fear and chaos among residents, including chasing children at bus stops and raiding wrong addresses.

headline: ACLU asks Bellmawr to investigate citations given to protesters
summary: The ACLU of New Jersey alleges that Bellmawr police may be infringing on protesters' First Amendment rights by issuing citations for minor offenses during antifascism rallies. The ACLU has requested an investigation into these practices, which could potentially impact future protests in the area if found to violate constitutional protections.

headline: OPINION: Nebraska fixed part of the school funding problem. But can it fix the new one it created?
summary: Nebraska's shift in school funding between 2022 and 2025 created two competing models: one favoring rural schools based on local needs and resources, the other providing flat-rate foundation aid. This has left lawmakers with a messy question of how to merge these systems into one fair system. Rural schools previously suffered under the TEEOSA formula due to surging farmland values but have since benefited from new funding streams bypassing the traditional formula. The state aims to fix its core formula or maintain two separate funding systems, impacting all public school districts statewide.

headline: States take the wheel in grizzly recovery
summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service proposes a new approach for species recovery under the Endangered Species Act. This approach allows states to gradually earn greater management authority as species populations meet recovery goals before full delisting, aiming to reduce conflict and incentivize conservation efforts while maintaining federal oversight. The grizzly bear population around Yellowstone National Park is used as an example, with over 1,000 bears now in the area after decades of collaborative effort. This proposal could potentially impact state budgets by shifting management responsibilities and associated costs from federal to state governments but does not specifically address budgetary implications.

headline: Federal judge dismisses Trump administration lawsuit against Washtenaw County’s sanctuary policies
summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit challenging Washtenaw County's "sanctuary policies," ruling that local governments can't be forced to enforce federal immigration laws beyond what is required by law. The county's policies, including not detaining individuals for ICE without judicial warrants and restricting federal immigration officers' access to county property, were upheld as constitutional under the Tenth Amendment.

headline: ‘The time for tolerance has ended’
summary: A once-popular principal was ousted from his rural Wisconsin school after a far-right majority on the school board, including Moms for Liberty members, spread false accusations of child grooming. The campaign led to protests and tension among parents, with some pulling their children out of the school.

headline: ICE arrests in Minnesota return to pre-surge levels while soaring nationwide
summary: After a surge of immigration arrests in Minnesota early this year, enforcement levels returned to pre-surge figures by July. Nationwide, ICE arrested nearly 50,000 immigrants in July, higher than any previous month under Trump's administration. Despite Minnesota initially ranking high in arrests, it dropped to 32nd by July.

headline: New court filings reveal more details of undercover agents’ surveillance of anti-ICE protesters
summary: The federal government has been surveilling anti-ICE activists in Minnesota, including tracking cars that followed ICE agents ("patrollers") and attendees at anti-ICE meetings. This extensive surveillance operation, involving undercover agents and electronic monitoring, was part of the Trump administration's efforts to curb resistance against immigration enforcement policies. The documents revealed in a federal case show frustration with these policies, which have led to harm for legal residents and deaths of American citizens.

headline: Minnesota set to fight in Texas courtroom to extradite ICE agent charged in Minneapolis shooting
summary: An ICE agent charged with shooting a Venezuelan man during Operation Metro surge faces extradition delays due to political disagreements between Minnesota's Democratic Gov. Tim Walz and Texas' Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, with Abbott refusing to sign extradition papers until Minnesota admits fault in social safety net fraud cases, potentially leading to Castro's release from custody as soon as Thursday.

headline: Demuth plans to cut $1 billion from Minnesota’s budget, refrains from denouncing tariffs
summary: Republican gubernatorial nominee Lisa Demuth proposes finding $1B in savings across state agencies to combat affordability issues. Her plan includes tax cuts for low-income residents and eliminating Social Security benefits taxation, potentially impacting Minnesota's two-year general fund budget of $66 billion.

headline: Judge in Minnesota extradition case “not inclined” to keep ICE officer jailed in Texas
summary: Minnesota Governor Tim Walz requested Texas Governor Greg Abbott to approve the extradition of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer held in Texas, highlighting tensions between states over immigration enforcement policies. Abbott has not yet made a decision on this request.

headline: Judge orders witness to Houston ICE shooting released from detention
summary: On July 14, ICE agent fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo at his home in Houston. This incident, which occurred during an enforcement operation, has raised concerns among local communities and officials about Immigration and Customs Enforcement's tactics and the impact on immigrant families.

headline: Abbott asks court to reject Minnesota bid to force extradition of ICE officer
summary: Governor Greg Abbott addressed immigration enforcement at the Texas State Republican Convention, emphasizing border security and criticizing Biden's border policies. He committed to continuing Texas' border surge operations, vowing to arrest migrants for state crimes before they're released by federal authorities.

headline: Mass. gives schools a playbook for ICE at the door
summary: The Massachusetts government has issued guidelines for schools and child care centers under its new immigrant protection law, requiring them to have policies governing interactions with civil immigration enforcement agents by September 1. The guidelines provide steps for handling ICE agent arrivals on site or information requests, protecting student privacy, and involving legal counsel when appropriate. This law aims to make schools safe learning spaces, free from warrantless immigration arrests, particularly in cities like Chelsea with high immigrant populations.

headline: Economists warn New Mexico fund subsidizing healthcare costs will soon run out of money
summary: New Mexico's Health Care Affordability Fund may face shortfalls of $85.3M by FY2028 and $273M by FY2030 due to rising premiums, federal cuts/changes driving more people to exchange. Legislative Finance Committee recommends reducing state subsidies for all recipients, potentially increasing low-income enrollment but resulting in coverage loss for those earning 600% or more of poverty level. State budget may need to allocate funds to cover projected shortfalls or adjust subsidy policies to maintain fiscal sustainability.

headline: McKee narrows gap but still trails Foulkes by 15 points in new WPRI poll
summary: According to a WPRI poll, Helena Buonanno Foulkes maintains a substantial lead over incumbent Gov. Dan McKee among Democratic primary voters (45% vs 30%), with 15 days left until the primary. Foulkes' record on opioids at CVS and McKee's handling of the Washington Bridge rebuild weigh heavily on voters' minds. McKee faces an uphill battle to close the gap, as Foulkes leads in almost every demographic category.

headline: Morrisey: 54K received school clothing allowance so far, including low-income kids who didn’t apply
summary: The West Virginia school clothing allowance program for low-income students faced delays and funding issues under Governor Morrisey, impacting around 54,000 children. Despite increased spending from federal TANF funds, the program's future sustainability is uncertain due to a looming deficit. While awaiting benefits, local mayor Chris Tatum raised funds to provide immediate clothing assistance to children in his area before school started.

headline: Pennsylvania reports nation’s first confirmed measles-related deaths in 2026
summary: The Pennsylvania Department of Health confirmed two measles-related deaths in Lancaster County among unvaccinated individuals, marking the first such deaths nationally this year amidst a record-breaking outbreak. The state will host pop-up vaccination clinics to combat the disease, which has infected nearly 400 Pennsylvanians across 29 counties so far in 2026.

headline: NC voters trust local elections more than national, poll shows
summary: North Carolinians have high confidence in local elections' security and integrity (70%), but confidence drops significantly for national elections (58%). They draw a distinction between direct election experience and those farther away. Most respondents (88%) value candidates accepting election results.

headline: Group behind whites-only community sues Arkansas, federal agencies
summary: White nationalist group 'Return to the Land' sues multiple agencies alleging violations of their rights by investigating a whites-only community they planned near Ravenden. The lawsuit claims retaliation against protected speech and association, but Arkansas' attorney general calls the claims meritless.

headline: Pritzker, Bailey offer different visions for Illinois education
summary: The Illinois State Board of Education approved a plan to fund schools based on student need. This new formula aims to allocate funds more equitably among districts.

headline: A Vermont teenager is holding the U.S. to its own law
summary: Vermont teenager Zoya Bianchi's letter criticizes U.S. aid to Israel amidst UN reports of genocide and human rights violations in Gaza Strip and Lebanon, sparking public debate on foreign policy.

headline: Virginia students make gains in reading, math as schools push toward pre-pandemic levels
summary: Virginia students' reading and math proficiency rates increased by 0.4% last year, marking progress towards pre-pandemic levels. Over five years, gains reached 5% in reading and 19% in math. New proficiency benchmarks have been implemented for this school year.
